documents.title: Emergency Department Physician Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Date of service: 03/07/2026 06:50
Carl Clark, 73 M

CC: chest pain, short of breath.

HPI: Woke with severe pressure behind the sternum about two hours before arrival, with breathlessness that has steadily worsened. Wife called EMS. Background: type 2 diabetes on oral medication, hypertension on lisinopril, hyperlipidemia, LVH, stage IV colon cancer with liver metastases on maintenance chemotherapy, postoperative AF in 2025.

Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily. NKDA.
SH: never smoker, no alcohol.

Vitals: T 37.5 C (99.5 F), HR 104, RR 28, BP 100/78, SpO2 88% on room air.

Exam: Anxious, speaking in short phrases. JVP elevated. Crackles throughout both lung fields. Tachycardic, regular; S3 and S4 present. No murmur. Abdomen soft. No leg swelling.

ECG: sinus tachycardia 104, LVH voltage, horizontal ST depression V3-V6, no ST elevation.
Portable CXR: bilateral perihilar infiltrates, mildly enlarged cardiac silhouette.
hs-Troponin I 1,850 ng/L. NT-proBNP 4,820 pg/mL.

ED course: BiPAP with improvement in work of breathing and saturation to 95%. Furosemide 40 mg IV. Aspirin 324 mg chewed. Heparin infusion started. Cardiology consulted at bedside.

Impression: acute non-ST elevation myocardial infarction with pulmonary edema.
Disposition: admitted to cardiac care unit.

Emergency Medicine

medications.reason: Stopped at hospital discharge; metoprolol started

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth daily (12 months after stent)

medications.drug: 24 HR metoprolol succinate 25 MG Extended Release Oral Tablet

medications.sig: Place 1 tablet under the tongue every 5 minutes as needed for chest pain, up to 3; call 911 if pain persists
Take 1 tablet by mouth daily for 5 days

reports.text: Complete study. Left ventricle normal in size with concentric left ventricular hypertrophy. Hypokinesis of the anterior wall. LVEF 50% (biplane). Right ventricle normal in size and function. Atria normal. Aortic, mitral, tricuspid and pulmonic valves without significant stenosis or regurgitation. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: Concentric LVH. Anterior wall hypokinesis with LVEF 50%. Normal valves. No pericardial effusion.

documents.title: Cardiac Catheterization Report
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
CARDIAC CATHETERIZATION LABORATORY
Date: 03/09/2026
Patient: Carl Clark, 73 M
Indication: NSTEMI.
Access: right radial artery, 6 Fr. Hemostasis with radial band.

Coronary angiography:
- Left main: no significant disease.
- LAD: 90% stenosis of the proximal segment. Distal vessel without significant disease.
- Left circumflex: 30% stenosis.
- RCA: 40% stenosis. Dominant.

Intervention: proximal LAD treated with one drug-eluting stent after predilation. 0% residual stenosis, TIMI 3 flow.

Conclusion: single-vessel culprit disease of the proximal LAD, treated with one DES. Nonobstructive disease of the circumflex and RCA.
Recommendations: aspirin indefinitely, clopidogrel for 12 months, high-intensity statin.

Interventional Cardiology

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 03/07/2026 via ED   Discharged 03/12/2026
Service: Cardiology

Diagnoses: Acute non-ST elevation myocardial infarction with acute pulmonary edema. Coronary artery disease, s/p DES to proximal LAD 3/9. Left ventricular hypertrophy. Type 2 diabetes. Hypertension. Hyperlipidemia. Stage IV colon adenocarcinoma with liver metastases.

Course: Presented with 2 hours of substernal pressure and dyspnea, hypoxemic to 88%, BP 100/78, with pulmonary edema on exam and chest film. ECG with ST depression V3-V6; hs-troponin I 1,850 rising to a peak of 16,400 ng/L; NT-proBNP 4,820. Treated with BiPAP, IV furosemide, aspirin and heparin; off BiPAP within 24 hours and on room air by 3/8. Angiography 3/9 via the radial artery: proximal LAD 90% treated with one drug-eluting stent; circumflex 30%, RCA 40%. Echo 3/9: concentric LVH, anterior hypokinesis, LVEF 50%, normal valves. Lisinopril held for the first day for soft pressures and then resumed. Metformin held around contrast and resumed 48 hours afterward. No arrhythmia on telemetry.

Oncology (inpatient consult): maintenance 5-FU/leucovorin to be held; outpatient oncology follow-up to decide next steps.

Discharge medications:
- Aspirin 81 mg daily (continue)
- Clopidogrel 75 mg daily x 12 months (NEW)
- Atorvastatin 80 mg daily (NEW)
- Metoprolol succinate 25 mg daily (NEW)
- Lisinopril 20 mg daily (continue)
- Metformin 1000 mg twice daily (continue)
- Furosemide 20 mg daily for 5 days, then stop (NEW)
- Nitroglycerin 0.4 mg SL as needed for chest pain (NEW)
- STOP amlodipine

Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: PCP within 1 week; cardiology 4-6 weeks; cardiac rehabilitation referral placed; oncology.

Cardiology

documents.title: Call from patient's wife
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Mrs. Clark called: Carl was taken by ambulance Saturday morning with chest pain and trouble breathing, told he had a heart attack. In the cardiac unit, breathing better, off the mask. Having a heart catheterization today. She asked us to cancel his visit tomorrow.

Cancelled 3/10 appt. Will book TCM visit once discharged. Records request sent. PCP informed.

documents.title: Transitional Care Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit after admission 3/7-3/12 for heart attack. Wife present. Discharge summary not yet received - history from them and the printed discharge instructions and medication list he brought.

Per paperwork: NSTEMI; catheterization 3/9 through the right wrist with one stent to the LAD; echo "pumping 50%". Fluid in the lungs at arrival, treated.

Since home: no chest pain, no nitro used. Breathing back to normal; sleeps flat. No palpitations. Finished the 5 days of furosemide yesterday. Wrist site fine. Walking short distances in the house and driveway. Scared but steady.

Medication reconciliation - our list still had amlodipine; per discharge list it was stopped. Updated:
- aspirin 81 daily
- clopidogrel 75 daily (12 months)
- atorvastatin 80 daily
- metoprolol succinate 25 daily
- lisinopril 20 daily
- metformin 1000 BID
- nitroglycerin 0.4 SL PRN
- amlodipine STOPPED; furosemide course done
- oncology has held his maintenance chemo
Reviewed each pill with wife; pill box redone. Nitro instructions reviewed: sit down, one tablet, may repeat every 5 min x2, call 911 if not gone after the first.

Exam: NAD. HR 60s, regular. BP fine. Lungs clear, no crackles. Heart RRR, S4, no murmur, no S3. JVP not raised. R radial site healed, radial pulse intact. No edema.

A/P:
1. NSTEMI s/p DES to proximal LAD; CAD - on DAPT, high-intensity statin, beta-blocker, ACE inhibitor. Cardiac rehab referral placed by hospital - wife will call to schedule. Cardiology f/u 4/14.
2. Pulmonary edema at presentation - resolved clinically.
3. HTN - controlled on lisinopril + metoprolol.
4. T2DM - metformin resumed.
5. Metastatic colon cancer - maintenance therapy on hold per oncology.
BMP today (recent diuretic). RTC 4-5 weeks.

TCM high complexity, 50 minutes.

documents.title: rehab
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Started cardiac rehab last week, 3 days a week. They are nice there. They asked if I can do yard work yet - raking, pushing the mower. I see the heart doctor next Tuesday.

documents.title: RE: rehab
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Great news about rehab. Light yard work is reasonable as long as you can talk while you do it; save heavy lifting and the push mower until you've talked with cardiology next week and the rehab team says your exercise tolerance is there. Stop and use your nitro if you get chest pressure.

No chest pain, no nitro use, no dyspnea, no palpitations. Taking all medications, no bleeding problems on aspirin + clopidogrel. No muscle aches on atorvastatin.

RTC June.

documents.title: Oncology Follow-up
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
MEDICAL ONCOLOGY - FOLLOW-UP
Visit 05/12/2026
Carl Clark, 73 M
Diagnosis: stage IV adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon, liver metastases. s/p right hemicolectomy 3/2025; FOLFOX x12 5/2025-10/2025; maintenance 5-FU/leucovorin from 11/11/2025, held since his NSTEMI in March 2026 (DES to LAD 3/9/2026).

Interval: recovering well from the MI; in cardiac rehab. No abdominal symptoms. Weight stable. ECOG 1.

CT A/P today: liver metastases stable, largest 2.3 cm; no new disease. CEA 6.4 ng/mL (5.9 in October).

Assessment/plan: disease controlled. Given the recent MI and stable disease we agreed on a formal treatment break - maintenance 5-FU/leucovorin discontinued. Surveillance CT and CEA every 3 months; next in August. Ondansetron no longer needed. Port flush every 6-8 weeks.

Allergies: NKDA.
Medical Oncology
